standard.title: Trade Interconnections at All Scales
standard.description: the ways that places and people are interconnected with other places through trade in goods and services, at all scales
standard.prior_knowledge: Students understand that places are interconnected through movement of people, goods and ideas (Y7-8). They have not examined the mechanisms and scale variations of trade interconnections systematically, nor traced how these change over time at local, national and global scales.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students examine how and why places are interconnected through trade in goods and services at local, national and global scales, and identify examples of how trade interconnections change over time.

nodes.label: Local trade: businesses selling and buying across places
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify products and services that businesses in their local area sell to or buy from other places
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least two products or services that local businesses sell to other places and at least two they buy from other places
nodes.typical_width: Examine a range of local businesses — identify what they sell to and buy from other places; explain what factors determine whether a business sells locally, nationally or globally
wider: Map the trade connections of three local businesses at different scales — compare the geographic extent of their interconnections
Investigate how local farmers' market products connect to local, national and global supply chains simultaneously
Examine how digital platforms (e.g. Etsy, eBay) have changed the scale at which local producers can trade

response_modes.reason: Starting with local examples makes the abstract concept of trade interconnection concrete. Examining multiple local businesses — not just one — gives students a range of scale experiences to compare.

success_criteria: Identifies at least two products/services local businesses sell to other places
Identifies at least two products/services local businesses buy from other places
Distinguishes between businesses trading locally, nationally and globally

nodes.label: National, regional and global trade interconnections
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can examine how and why places are interconnected nationally, regionally and globally through trade in goods and services
nodes.minimum_width: Identify how places are interconnected through trade at national, regional and global scales; explain at least two reasons why places trade across scales
nodes.typical_width: Explain why places specialise in particular goods or services and how comparative advantage, resource endowment and market demand drive trade interconnections at national, regional and global scales; give examples from Australia and its trading partners
wider: Analyse why Australia exports particular goods (iron ore, coal, agricultural products) but imports others — explain using resource endowment and comparative advantage
Examine regional trade agreements (e.g. ASEAN, Pacific trade agreements) — explain how agreements shape the geography of trade interconnections
Investigate the role of global cities (e.g. Singapore, Hong Kong) as trade hubs — explain how their location and infrastructure concentrate trade interconnections
nodes.hinge_reason: Understanding why places trade — comparative advantage, resource endowment, market demand — is prerequisite for explaining how interconnections change over time in Node 3 and why production impacts fall where they do in K08. Students who can only describe that trade happens without explaining why cannot trace the logic of changing interconnections.

response_modes.reason: The 'how and why' framing in the descriptor signals that description alone is insufficient. Students who list trade examples without explaining the mechanisms (why does Australia export iron ore rather than steel?) cannot answer the 'why' component. Scaffolding the comparative advantage and resource endowment logic builds the explanatory depth the descriptor requires.

Covering local, national, regional and global scales prevents students from conflating scale levels. Each scale has different trade logic, and students who understand only one level cannot generalise.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The trade hub/global city direction is rich — Singapore and Hong Kong have become concentrated nodes in global trade networks due to specific geographic, political and infrastructural factors. Advancing students who examine a trade hub gain insight into how geographic advantage and political history shape trade interconnections in ways that purely economic explanations miss.
success_criteria: Identifies trade interconnections at national, regional and global scales
Explains at least two reasons why places trade at different scales
Gives specific examples from Australia's trade relationships

nodes.label: Change in trade interconnections over time
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify examples of change in interconnections between places and people through trade over time at local, national and global scales
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least one example of how trade interconnections have changed over time at the local, national and global scale
nodes.typical_width: Explain how and why trade interconnections have changed over time at local, national and global scales — consider how changing technologies, geopolitics, environmental conditions or consumer preferences have altered trade relationships; give examples at each scale
wider: Trace how a specific trade relationship has changed over time (e.g. Australia-China trade in resources or food) — explain what drove the change and how it affected both places
Examine how global supply chain restructuring during COVID-19 altered trade interconnections — what changed at local, national and global scales?
Investigate how environmental factors (e.g. climate change, resource depletion) are beginning to alter the geography of trade interconnections

response_modes.reason: Change over time is best understood through specific cases at each scale. Students who generalise without grounding in a specific case ('trade has globalised') cannot explain why particular interconnections changed. Covering at least one example at each scale level anchors the generalisation.

success_criteria: Identifies at least one example of changed trade interconnection at local, national and global scales
Explains what drove the change in each case
